```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Global knitr options: hide code by default (a supervisor sees plots, not
# code), and suppress package start-up noise from the plot chunks.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7,
  dpi = 110,
  dev = if (requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) "svglite" else "svg"
)

# here::here() anchors every path to the repository root (drug_policy_spectrum.Rproj),
# so this knits and also runs chunk-by-chunk from a fresh session.
library(here)

# The data layer builds `pilot` and everything the tabs use.
source(here("analysis", "reports", "descriptive_plots", "data.R"))
# cached chunks are keyed to the data they read
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache.extra = tools::md5sum(unlist(DELIVERY[c("completed", "in_progress")])))
```

<script>
/* ---- top-level tabs ---- */
function showTab(name){
  ['report','involvement','analysis'].forEach(function(t){
    document.getElementById('pane-' + t).style.display =
      (t === name) ? '' : 'none';
    document.getElementById('tabbtn-' + t).classList.toggle('active', t === name);
  });
  if(window.showPaneToc) showPaneToc(name);
}

/* ---- a contents list in the sidebar for every tab ----
   tocify builds ONE flat TOC for the whole document: its hierarchy runs
   straight through the tab boundaries, so while the report tab was open the
   sidebar listed the analysis and appendix sections too, and on the other tabs
   those sections were nested under a report heading and unreachable.
   Rather than fight tocify's tree, EVERY pane - the report included - gets its
   own list built from its own headings, and tocify's own lists stay hidden.
   Each tab then shows exactly its own sections and nothing else.

   Headings only appear here if they carry an id. Pandoc gives one to every
   markdown heading; the raw-HTML <h1>/<h2> that open each pane have theirs
   written out by hand for that reason. */
(function(){
  var toc = document.getElementById('TOC');
  if(!toc) return;

  function build(pane){
    var heads = pane.querySelectorAll('h1:not(.toc-ignore), h2:not(.toc-ignore)');
    var ul = document.createElement('ul');
    ul.className = 'pane-toc list-group';
    ul.style.display = 'none';
    heads.forEach(function(h){
      if(!h.id) return;
      var a = document.createElement('a');
      a.href = '#' + h.id;
      a.textContent = h.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
      var li = document.createElement('li');
      li.className = 'list-group-item' + (h.tagName === 'H2' ? ' sub' : '');
      li.appendChild(a);
      ul.appendChild(li);
    });
    if(!ul.children.length) return null;   // a pane without headings: no list
    toc.appendChild(ul);
    return ul;
  }

  var lists = {};
  ['report','involvement','analysis'].forEach(function(t){
    lists[t] = build(document.getElementById('pane-' + t));
  });

  var current = null;
  window.showPaneToc = function(name){
    // tocify emits one top-level <ul> PER h1, not a single tree, and none of
    // them is wanted now that every pane has its own list. They are hidden
    // HERE rather than once at setup: this script runs while the document is
    // still parsing, and tocify does not build those <ul>s until jQuery's
    // ready event, so anything hidden at setup would simply reappear.
    toc.querySelectorAll(':scope > ul:not(.pane-toc)').forEach(function(u){
      u.style.display = 'none';
    });
    Object.keys(lists).forEach(function(t){
      if(lists[t]) lists[t].style.display = (t === name) ? '' : 'none';
    });
    current = lists[name] || null;
    // a pane with no headings at all gets no sidebar
    toc.style.display = current ? '' : 'none';
    mark();
  };

  // the report tab is the one open on load; wait for tocify to have built its
  // lists before hiding them
  window.addEventListener('load', function(){ showPaneToc('report'); });

  // highlight the section currently at the top of the screen, the way tocify
  // does on the report tab
  function mark(){
    if(!current) return;
    var items = current.querySelectorAll('li'), best = -1;
    items.forEach(function(li, i){
      var h = document.getElementById(li.querySelector('a').getAttribute('href').slice(1));
      if(h && h.getBoundingClientRect().top <= 120) best = i;
    });
    items.forEach(function(li, i){ li.classList.toggle('active', i === best); });
  }
  window.addEventListener('scroll', mark);
})();

/* ---- involvement bimodality browser ----
   Moved to involvement_browser.js and inlined by
   involvement.Rmd, which is where its data comes from. */

</script>
```

```{r dataset-checks, echo=TRUE}
# Invariants of the analysis dataset. These are cheap and they fail the knit
# loudly, which is what you want if new data or a reworded question ever
# breaks an assumption the rest of the report is built on.
stopifnot(
  # one row per analysed respondent, no duplicates
  nrow(pilot) == n_pilot,
  !anyDuplicated(pilot$ResponseId),
  # every item block is present and complete
  all(item_meta$variable %in% names(pilot)),
  all(paste0(item_meta$variable, "_scored") %in% names(pilot)),
  all(POLICY_COLUMNS %in% names(pilot)),
  length(select_items("betrokkenheid",   names(pilot))) == 5L,
  length(subst_cols) == 4L,
  # reverse-scoring is its own inverse on the flipped items, and a no-op elsewhere
  all.equal(pilot[[reverse_cols[1]]],
            (SCALE_MIN + SCALE_MAX) - pilot[[paste0(reverse_cols[1], "_scored")]]),
    # an item the pool calls "Pro" is not flipped: its _scored copy is the raw
  # answer. Taken from item_meta rather than named, because the two pilots do
  # not share item names.
  identical(pilot[[item_meta$variable[item_meta$reverse_coded == "no"][1]]],
            pilot[[paste0(item_meta$variable[item_meta$reverse_coded == "no"][1],
                          "_scored")]])
)
cat("`pilot`:", nrow(pilot), "respondents x", ncol(pilot),
    "columns - all checks passed.\n")
